source: Self-Improving AI Coding Agents Through Accumulated Behavioral Rules (arXiv:2607.13091)
summary: Microsoft researchers show that converting accepted code-review comments into versioned behavioral rules yields 0% recurrence for covered error classes across 35+ microservices. Rules live in a version-controlled instruction file; model weights never change.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps directly to skill distillation (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). AgentForge already ships this pattern; the remaining gap (executor prompts not receiving skills) is tracked by HID-188.

source: Self-Evolving Coding Rules for AI Coding Agents / RuleEvolve (arXiv:2610.00650)
summary: Proposes RuleEvolve, an automatic method for evolving coding-agent behavioral rules from execution outcomes without manual labeling.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — same theme as 2607.13091 and AgentForge's shipped distillation system. No new gap identified beyond HID-188.

source: SpecForge: Recursive Self-Improvement via Behavioral Specifications (arXiv:2610.15708)
summary: Multi-frontier tree search that improves an agent's behavioral specification (not model weights) recursively using Pareto-guided state selection and error-diversified expansion.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires a spec-centric agent architecture incompatible with AgentForge's CLI subprocess model. Too research-focused; no clear 1-2 run implementation path.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel successor)
summary: Microsoft released MAF 1.0 (April 2026) as the unified successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel. Supports sequential, concurrent, group-chat, handoff, and Magentic orchestration with checkpointing and human-in-the-loop.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — API-client-based .NET/Python framework. AgentForge uses CLI subprocess agents; patterns like checkpointing are already native to AgentForge's state machine. Architecture is fundamentally incompatible.

source: ContextBudget: Budget-Aware Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents (arXiv:2604.01664)
summary: Treats context compression as a sequential decision problem under a fixed context window, using RL with a tightened budget curriculum. Adapts compression aggressively as remaining capacity shrinks.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly relevant once HID-163 (token/cost telemetry) ships. Explicitly blocked by CLAUDE.md until measurement infrastructure exists.

source: LangMem layered memory architecture for LangGraph agents (2026)
summary: LangMem provides semantic (user facts), episodic (interaction summaries), and procedural (agent instructions) memory layers on top of LangGraph's checkpointer. Integrates with Mem0 for cross-session recall.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge ships semantic/procedural skill memory via distillationAgent.ts. Cross-run episodic memory injection is tracked by HID-188. No new gap identified.

source: Mendel Gödel Machine: Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution (arXiv:2608.07645)
summary: Agents that rewrite their own codebase via comparative fitness evolution, eliminating the meta-agent/target-agent distinction.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — recursive self-modification of the orchestrator itself is too speculative and risky for a production system. No feasible 1-2 run implementation path.

summary: Comparative benchmark of 13 agent frameworks on a five-agent travel-planning workflow run 100 times each. Finds overhead does not predict speed; model selection matters more than framework choice.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — benchmark data only, no actionable pattern for AgentForge. Confirms sequential determinism (AgentForge's design) is competitive with parallel orchestrators on typical workloads.

source: Karpathy 2026: Agents, Autoresearch, and the Self-Improvement Loopy Era
summary: Karpathy describes 'autoresearch' agents running 700+ experiments autonomously, and his shift to ~80% AI-generated code. Notes current models act as 'sloppy junior developers' needing structured guardrails.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — validates AgentForge's structured state machine approach as a guardrail pattern. 'Sloppy junior developer' framing reinforces value of plan approval gates and AI review stages.
